subject: ZenHealth Private Offer — buyer approvals & subscription duration
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Samir Gupta <samir.gupta@zenhealth.com>, Sophie Tillman <sophie.tillman@zenhealth.com>
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: ZenHealth Private Offer — buyer approvals & subscription duration

Hi Samir / Sophie,

Thanks for taking the time on Tuesday. As promised, I'm outlining three configurable paths for the private offer so you can run this by procurement:

1) 12-month subscription (annual billing) — standard buyer approval (procurement + BU finance).
2) 24-month subscription (annual billing split) — requires CFO approval for multi-year commitments.
3) 3-month pilot (monthly billing) — eligible for self-serve activation, low-touch approval (technical signoff only).

For each option we can set meter vs. committed-usage pricing. Attached is a short summary showing expected unit economics across your projected usage (ZenHealth_AWS_PO_Term_Summary.pdf). Can you confirm which path you'd like us to thread through your approvals, and whether you need a buyer-specific approval matrix from us to submit to procurement?

If helpful, we can also include a one-sheet mapping who in ZenHealth needs to sign at each dollar threshold.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0142

Attachment: ZenHealth_AWS_PO_Term_Summary.pdf (1 page, PDF)

Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ZenHealth Private Offer — buyer approvals & subscription duration

Stephanie — thanks for the breakdown. A few quick procurement questions so I can route this internally: 

- For the 24-month option, does Redwood require an upfront commit or will you accept annual invoicing?
- What is the threshold that would escalate to our CFO vs. our Director of Procurement? (we have $250k set as senior approval historically)
- Can you provide a short evidence bundle showing SOC2 scope and data residency controls to attach to our procurement ticket?

Also looping in Sophie who will own procurement routing.

Thanks,
Samir
Director of Platform Engineering
ZenHealth
samir.gupta@zenhealth.com

Vivek / Ben — forwarding procurement questions from ZenHealth (Samir + Sophie). Key asks: upfront commit vs annual invoicing for 24 months, approval dollar threshold (customer indicates $250k to CFO), and SOC2/data residency evidence bundle.

Notes / proposed approach: 
- We can accept annual invoicing on the 24-month term; upfront commit is optional but gives them better unit pricing. Offer: upfront 20% discount vs annual invoices.
- Approval threshold: recommend we map our private offer activation gates to the buyer's internal threshold. If total ARR > $250k, we'll require CFO counter-sign; else procurement + BU finance OK.
- Evidence: Attach standard SOC2 package and our regional data flow summary. Ben, can you confirm we can bundle the regional residency note for US-only processing? Vivek, any concerns on discounting or deal structure?

Would like to send consolidated reply to Samir by EOD today.

Thanks,
Stephanie

Attachment: ZenHealth_approval_matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Stephanie — agree with the approach. Quick answers to feed back to Samir: 

- 24-month: we will accept annual invoicing by default. Upfront pre-pay is optional. If they pre-pay, offer an additional 12% effective unit discount (we've run this on similar deals).
- Thresholds: confirm we use $250k as the CFO escalation point. We'll include a one-page approval matrix (who signs at what tiers) that Samir can attach to his procurement ticket.
- Evidence: SOC2 summary + data residency page for US-region processing are cleared; attaching the short bundle for ZenHealth.

I'll let you finalize language. Happy to hop on a quick call if they push on multi-year billing.

Best,
Ben Carter
Head of Marketplace Sales Operations
